sections.overview: The Taiwan blue magpie is a corvid endemic to Taiwan.
sections.identification: It has a black head, red bill and feet, a blue body, and a very long tail with white tips.
sections.habitat: It inhabits broad-leaved and secondary forests at low and middle elevations, including wooded areas near people.
sections.diet: It is omnivorous, eating fruit, seeds, insects and small vertebrates.
sections.behavior: It often travels in groups, sometimes flying in a conspicuous line of long-tailed birds.
sections.reproduction: It nests high in trees and typically lays four to six eggs; other group members may help feed the young.
sections.ecology: Its cooperative helpers are a notable part of its social breeding system.
sections.conservation: Taiwan’s National Museum describes it as protected; a local scenic-area account identifies habitat disturbance and loss as concerns.
